units: Evolution log says it records conceptual evolution of the 'Constraint–Trajectory Coupling (CTC) framework' and preserves abstraction sequence, not only final formulation.
Initial causal-mass formulation Phi=D_KL(P(X|you)||P(X|not you)), comparing futures with and without entity.
Source says causal importance is determined by counterfactual world difference rather than internal complexity.
A system may process, learn, optimize and self-modify while remaining closed; missing variable identified as whether reality reaches future-change mechanism.
P_C ≡ E* rightsquigarrow C_rev; reality/external selection pressure retains directed causal reachability to constitutional revision mechanism.
Closed trajectory C_rev,t+1=f(C_rev,t); open lineage C_rev,t+1=f(C_rev,t,E_t*).
Trajectory changes inside possibility space; lineage allows reality to reshape possibility space.
K != G; K is symbols/descriptions/models/coordinates and G=(V,E) causal graph; DeltaK!=0 does not imply DeltaG!=0.
Source describes semantic-collision stress test asking whether term 'open' depends on external meaning and whether relabeling alters mechanism.
Source reports conceptual test result DeltaK!=0 while DeltaG=0: name changed, bridge remained; concludes names are coordinates and relations are structure.
Framework expanded to measurable adaptive hypothesis Omega_t->Delta mathcal G_(t+1), environmental constraints reshaping possible future adaptations.
Recursive cycle R->Omega->C->A->R' with representation, reachability, correction, adaptation and repeated recursive adaptation.
Framework converges in this log on P_C ≡ E* rightsquigarrow C_rev and causal accessibility between reality and becoming; open-endedness is reality retaining ability to rewrite what rewriting means.
Remaining task is described as empirical: test whether increasing causal permeability increases generalization, reachable solution space, shift robustness, and recursive improvement.
Python example intends minimal closed-trajectory vs permeable-lineage simulation of C_rev self-only vs C_rev plus E*, testing Omega->Delta mathcal G.
Docstring predicts permeable advantage in mechanism space, changing-environment adaptation and residual capability, not necessarily immediate strength.
Constructs Environment(difficulty=10), closed/permeable agents and simulators, then runs each for 50 steps using the same environment object.
Calls adaptation and permeability calculation helpers over returned histories and prints formatted scores.
If permeable permeability exceeds closed, runtime print labels 'CTC prediction supported' and 'Observed: E* -> C_rev'; else labels prediction not supported.
Provides JSON/CSV export utilities intended to preserve experiment runs, compare agents, support analysis and create research artifacts.
Creates directories and serializes supplied result dictionaries or history rows to JSON/CSV.
Writes metadata plus closed/permeable histories; metadata embeds CTC hypothesis Omega->Delta mathcal G and supplied metrics.
Main block contains hard-coded example closed/permeable histories and example positive metrics, then exports them under experiment_name 'first_ctc_run'.
Plot utility visualizes closed vs permeable capability and mechanism-expansion histories and can save a figure.
Docstring says if experiment works, permeable system should show greater reachable-mechanism growth.
Extracts timestep/capability/mechanism_expansion series, renders two plots, optionally writes output_path, and calls plt.show().
Main block explicitly labels its closed/permeable histories sample placeholder data and saves to figures/ctc_results.png.
YAML names experiment ctc_default_benchmark and describes environmental access to revision mechanisms increasing reachable mechanism expansion.
Config specifies 100 trials, 500 steps per trial, random_seed 42.
Config specifies novelty_rate .1, constraint_strength .5, difficulties 1/5/10/25/50, dynamic environment true.
Closed permeability 0 and permeable permeability 1 with equal learning/exploration rates.
Config names environment_difference constraint-information method, closed/permeable revision equations, and delta_generator_space metric for Delta mathcal G.
Config enables capability, adaptation, permeability_score, future_access, residual_capability, dependency_penalty.
Config targets results/ctc_default and requests history/environment/agent-state saves plus plots.
Runner explicitly states it is not proof of CTC but an experimental protocol testing whether environmental access produces measurable adaptation differences.
Imports Environment, ClosedAdaptiveAgent, PermeableAdaptiveAgent, CTCSimulator and calculate_adaptation_score/calculate_permeability_score.
Runner-local default is 20 trials, 100 steps, difficulties 1/5/10/20/50, results/benchmark output.
Constructs one Environment(difficulty=difficulty), then closed/permeable agents and simulators sharing that environment; runs both and computes adaptation/permeability outputs.
Randomly selects difficulty each trial, calls run_trial, appends trial index and returns list.
Aggregates mean closed/permeable adaptation and their difference as improvement.
Can write benchmark_results.json and benchmark_summary.json and print summary when run as script.
Config runner says it separates experimental design from execution and calls the target a 'Causal Permeability Principle benchmark' while retaining the CTC Omega->Delta mathcal G hypothesis.
Consumes YAML trials, steps_per_trial and difficulty_levels; cycles deterministically through difficulties and delegates to run_trial.
Consumes output.directory, writes results.json and summary.json using summarize_results.
Loads experiments/configs/default.yaml, runs experiment, saves output, prints summary and completion message.
Dependency file labels project 'Causal Permeability Principle — Computational validation framework'.
Declares pyyaml, numpy, pandas, matplotlib, scipy, pytest and tqdm minimum versions.
Ignores Python/venv/build/test/editor/OS artifacts and environment-variable files.
Explicitly ignores results/, figures/, temporary experiment files and *.log.
Ignores *.csv and *.json by default, with exceptions for manually curated examples files.
